recovery.plan: touch_main.cpp: once the bus has been idle, a line held low 30 ms restarts the whole XIAO; Wire.begin is retried every 100 ms until it succeeds; task watchdog; RS restart, RD pause and HD/HC hold commands; serial never blocks. walk_wired.py sends RS after 10 failed reads. Firmware bugs found and fixed 2026-10-31 while testing it: (1) the core's slave init refuses to start while a line is low and never retries, so a restart during a held line or during the A7Z's boot left the slave dead (069aec6a and f629c8c0 in the robot; reproduced by holding SCL 200 ms: 0 of 25 reads; fixed: 25 of 25); (2) with USB plugged in and the Mac's port closed each serial write waited 2 s and the task watchdog restarted the XIAO (fixed with setTxTimeoutMs(0), 86f9f7c7). During T1 the XIAO runs the original firmware; the new build is reflashed after it.

cause.evidence: Mechanism (19:19-19:27): a bit error on the line (first error always 'Arbitration lost') leaves the XIAO's slave a few bits out of step, driving SDA low and waiting for clocks; the sunxi driver never clocks it out, so the jam lasts until power-off. Onset: all three jammed boots had microphone capture running 2-6 min before the jam (16:30:18 -> 16:33:35, 17:11:30 -> 17:17:40, 19:17 -> 19:19:14); 16:58-17:11 without capture read fine. Shawn's hand on the head (19:28:50-19:29:27, pads 23.6k -> 30.5k, A7Z idle) gave 0 errors; mid-read pauses up to 3 s gave none (H2 ruled out). Capture alone (19:39:03-19:44:10 A7Z clock, arecord 4 ch + aplay keepalive, no brain, new firmware): 0 kernel errors in 5 min, one byte-shift at 19:42:09 (Shawn was hot-gluing the microphone backs in the head that hour). Then 19:44:22-19:47:05 another session's snap-test capture with Shawn's hands at the head (pads to 31k at 19:45:45) and, from 19:45:39, a brain in stand with torque on: 3 full onsets and 5 short ACK/STOP errors. Hand alone (no capture, no brain): 0. So no single factor triggers it here; capture with a hand at the head and/or a running brain does. Separating test queued in T1.

hypotheses.claim: In walk mode at KP 200 the policy holds the knees with goals far ahead of the positions (2026-11-12: right knee goal 2699 against position 2513, left 1355 against 1598, i.e. 186 and 244 ticks = 16 and 21 deg, currents 94 and -128 mA). Stand entry keeps those goals as the ramp start (walk_brain.py: start = self.goal or q) and doubles the gain on the same tick, so the knee torque doubles at once.
hypotheses.status: supported by the 11-12 log: on the two ticks after the switch the knee currents rose to 224 and -351 mA with unchanged goals, the knees moved 90 and 115 ticks (8 and 10 deg) in 0.15 s, and the body pitch followed (gyro y -0.7 rad/s at 0.07 s, gravity x -0.28 at 0.3 s). The ramp itself had moved the goals 2 ticks by then.

tests.what: Stand entry from a policy mode starts the ramp from position + (goal - position) * KP_walk / KP_stand, so the torque is the same on the first tick; check in brain_sim_check.py with a walk-to-stand switch after standing on the policy, then on the robot with Shawn's hand near it.
tests.status: sim run 2026-11-12 (Mac mini ~/sims/standsw, asbuilt current, 7.6 V, old code = commit f8ba3253): switch after standing on the policy without a step: old code tilts 2.6 deg within 0.2 s and falls later (36.8 s), new code stays at 0.0 deg and stands to the end (53 s, max tilt 0.9). Switch after a 3.6 s walk: old falls 2.6 s after the switch, new 4.8 s after it, both backward and not on the switch tick. Correction 2026-11-12: the earlier note that the robot made this switch several times that day without falling has no log behind it (the five robot log slices hold two walk-to-stand switches: the 22:02 fall and one with the robot held in the hand). Sim study the same evening: the sim's open-loop stand has its centre of mass 5.0 mm behind the ankle axis and drifts backward (1.5 deg/min) even without a walk; the robot's ankle goal leads and currents in stand show a centre of mass about 2-3 mm further forward (+-1 mm); a +1.5 mm trial shift (--com-x) made the sim stand in every case tried. No model change made: which part's mass or position is wrong is not identified (battery-20261104 is unweighed). In walk_brain.py and copied to the A7Z (takes effect at the next brain start); not yet switched on the robot.

hypotheses.status: open: the 11-02 event followed a logged flat pack; for 11-13 the rail history before the boot has not been read (A7Z offline when it was tried). Shawn 2026-11-13, a guess, not an observation: "可能是电池放空过，我猜". Supporting evidence 2026-11-19: one Tattu 2S 650 has a cell that will not charge (B3 charger photo IMG_7387: cell 1 green full, cell 2 red forever) and on the robot lights the OpenRB but not the A7Z (pack under the DFR1202's 6 V minimum input), so that pack was deeply discharged at least once. Chain: pack under 6 V -> DFR1202 drops the A7Z -> brain and battery guard stop -> OpenRB and 15 servos (about 0.26 A standby) stay on the switch and drain the pack slowly through the servo brownout range. Not yet tied to a dated occurrence.
